key_insight: FlatManifold turns continual learning into a more robust optimization problem by flattening data geometry in RKHS, which helps resist both severe label noise and domain shifts.
engineering_relevance: This offers a streamlined alternative to complex sample-filtering pipelines for robotics and other streaming systems that must keep learning under changing conditions.
method: Nyström-based manifold flattening with the kernel trick to map features into an orthogonalized RKHS.
Ridge-regularized projection onto a fixed target topology to smooth the effect of noisy labels.
A continual topology brake term using past covariance to reduce catastrophic forgetting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong results on real-world multi-session robotics datasets, including 40% symmetric label noise and cross-session seasonal/lighting shifts, where the method outperforms sequential baselines.
watch_item: The approach may depend on kernel/Nyström design and covariance tracking, which can be sensitive to memory, scalability, and hyperparameter choices in large streaming deployments.
paper_title: FlatManifold: Robust Continual Learning under Severe Label Noise and Domain Shifts via Intrinsic Manifold Flattening
